family.unavailablePolicy: Unavailable hypotheses retain a p=1 slot for family correction and remain null in displayed results.
family.resolutionScope: Theoretical smallest first Holm-adjusted value for this family and reference budget; ties can raise the attainable minimum. This is not a significance or outcome claim.

method.statistic: Absolute Spearman correlation using midranks; two-sided in correlation sign
method.orientation: The lexicographically later series ID is rotated, independent of displayed column order.
method.denominator: One identity orientation plus every unique selected nonidentity rotation; ties count as at least as extreme.
method.probabilityMeaning: Reference probability under a uniformly rotated finite periodic series; not a calibrated real-world event probability.
assumptions: Complete series on a strictly increasing equal-UTC grid
Uniform relative circular phase is the explicitly artificial reference model
No claim of stationarity, valid periodic boundary or independence of calendar rules
All selected pairs belong to the correction family before any result is displayed

limitations: All series are calculations on the declared finite sampling grid. Correlation and exceedance frequency are not probabilities of wars, illness, financial performance or other real-world outcomes.
Calendar labels and rules can share the same Sun, Moon, clock or arithmetic. A strong correlation can be an expected mathematical dependency rather than independent corroboration.

The circular-phase reference assumes a uniformly selected relative rotation on a finite periodic grid. It preserves each complete series and its circular ordering but changes cross-series phase; this artificial model is not established as a data-generating mechanism.

Equal UTC spacing and complete data are necessary eligibility checks here, not proof of stationarity or of the periodic wrap boundary. Trends, annual seasonality, discontinuities and endpoint mismatch can make the reference scientifically inappropriate.

Holm adjustment uses every pair in this requested family, including unavailable pairs as conservative family slots. It does not correct for earlier runs, changed date windows, selected locations, thresholds, alternative rules or undisclosed searches.

A fixed natal map is constant through a date scan; its correlation and phase-reference probability are unavailable. Time-varying map calculations must be explicitly identified as event or transit maps.

scope: Finite daily-grid illustration. Correlations and phase-reference fractions concern calculated series, not the probability of life or geopolitical events. Criteria were not selected using these results. Runtime comparison is observational, with different warm-cache states and extra brute guidance work; not an isolated performance experiment.
